title: Signal-sculpting release orchestration: three-phase schedule & handoff notebook
content:
Purpose:
This notebook captures a pragmatic, three-phase release pattern we want to try for the next inference runtime / routing change. The emphasis is on sculpting request traffic (signal shaping), warming caches, and staged model-variant fallbacks so we can keep latency SLOs while validating correctness and cost profiles. This doc is a working draft — intended for the release owner and ops crew to iterate against during preflight.

Release objective (succinct):
- Validate new routing policy that prefers quantized model variants for non-critical routes while keeping critical routes pinned to high-precision variants.
- Maintain p95 latency <= 220ms for critical routes and p95 <= 320ms for non-critical routes during steady-state.
- No regression in top-5 intent accuracy for seeded eval set.

High-level approach (signal-sculpting):
- Phase 0 (Prep / Dry-run): internal traffic only, synthetic load generator with weave of short/long sequences, KV prefix warmups, smoke tests of fallback logic.
- Phase 1 (Softlaunch / Funnel): 1% of production requests for 3h -> 5% for 2h, enforce strict canary guardrails (telemetry, user-impact telemetry, error budget).
- Phase 2 (Staggered Ramp to Steady): increment by ~10% every hour, with automated pause if latency or error gates trip.

T0 conventions and naming:
- T0 = first minute of Phase 1 (softlaunch start).
- Canary namespace: release-sculpt-v2026-05-3
- Rollowner: diego.m@redwood.com (Diego Morales)

Preflight checklist (Phase 0 items, all must be green before T0):
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards deployed and baseline captured (latency, error rate, token throughput, cost-per-token).
- [ ] Canary routing rules loaded into the router with explicit fallback mapping for each route.
- [ ] Synthetic workload scripts (short/long ratio 70/30) validated against staging cluster.
- [ ] KV cache warmup recipe verified for top-100 prefixes in production traffic sample.
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed by SRE and QA, handoff sign-off obtained.
- [ ] On-call rotation assigned for the 24h post-roll period (primary, secondary, triage).
- [ ] Slack status channel reserved (#release-sculpting-watch) and Statuspage pre-draft prepared.

Phase 1 (Softlaunch) detailed steps and gates:
- 00:00 - T0: open softlaunch funnel -> 1% traffic. Verify: p95 latency and error rate within 10% of baseline, no increase in user-visible failures.
- 00:30 - 1st telemetry check: confirm prefix hit rates, KV cache effectiveness, and that quantized variant is serving expected percent of non-critical calls.
- 01:30 - if health OK, increase to 5%. If any gate trips (p95 > threshold, error spike, or eval accuracy drop), immediately pause and roll to fallback.
- 03:00 - run seeded eval against a mirror of production prompts; collect quality diffs.

Phase 2 (Staggered ramp) operations runbook:
- Ramp cadence: +10% per hour starting from 5% until 60%, then +20% steps to 100% if stable.
- Automated gate checks at each step:
  - latency.p95.critical <= 220ms and latency.p95.noncritical <= 320ms
  - total.error-rate.delta <= 0.5% absolute
  - seeded-eval.top5-accuracy.delta <= 1.5% relative
- If a gate trips, rollback to prior stable percentage and run root-cause collection checklist (logs, flamegraphs, slow-query dumps).

Operator quick-checklist (day-of):
- [ ] Read T-12h preflight summary from diego.m
- [ ] Ensure smoke tests in staging have 0 failures in last 2 hours
- [ ] Confirm on-call list and escalation links
- [ ] Keep an eye on KV cache hit ratio dashboard and slot warming curve
- [ ] Watch routing decision logs for unexpected route churn (more than 0.2% per 5m)

Release notes draft (to be published after Phase 2 completion):
Title: Sculpted routing and quantized-variant rollout (v2026-05-3)
What changed:
- Introduced a routing policy that routes low-priority non-interactive routes to quantized variants (q8_0) while preserving high-precision models for critical interactive endpoints.
- Added KV prefix warmup to reduce cold-start token latency for common prompts.
- New circuit-breaker heuristics for early fallback on sustained latency increases.
Impact:
- Expected ~18% reduction in token compute cost for noncritical traffic at steady-state.
- No intended change to user-visible model outputs; seeded eval shows minor quality delta within acceptable guardrails.
Rollout schedule (summary):
- May 3 2026: softlaunch and ramp; observed metrics included in postmortem.

Rollback and mitigation matrix (quick reference):
- Symptom: p95 latency regression in critical routes > 10%
  Action: Immediately hit manual rollback -> route all critical routes to pinned high-precision cluster, pause ramp, notify SRE.
- Symptom: seeded-eval top5-quality delta > 2%
  Action: Pause, reduce to 0% for affected routes, trigger QA review of model variant mapping.
- Symptom: spike in 5xxs > baseline + 0.5%
  Action: Auto-fallback rule engages (quantized->fallback variant), escalate to primary on-call.

Telemetry knobs and thresholds (explicit):
- latency.p95.critical: 220ms (hard); alert at 210ms (warning) during ramp step.
- error.rate.total: baseline + 0.5% absolute -> alert.
- kv.cache.hit: warn if drop > 6% compared to baseline for 15m window.
- route-churn: warn if >0.2% of routed requests change target variant within 5m window.

Communication templates (publish in Slack and Status):
- Slack (T0): "[release-sculpt-v2026-05-3] Phase 1 start. 1% traffic. Rollowner Diego Morales. Watch #release-sculpting-watch. If you see p95-critical >210ms tag @sre-oncall immediately."
- Status page (post rollout): short blurb summarizing feature and impact (cost/latency).

Post-release quick retro (initial items to capture within 24h):
- How accurate were our traffic forecasts vs observed?
- Which prefixes had the slowest warmup and why?
- Was route-churn higher than simulated? Causes?
- Any telemetry blindspots discovered?

Open questions / To resolve before next attempt:
- Should we gate K-sampling (requests sent to quantized variant) by request-size in tokens (e.g., only apply q8 to requests < 256 tokens)?
- Is there a cheap server-side deterministic sample we can add to synthesize more realistic cache warmups for tail prefixes?
- Verify estimated cost reduction with finance for committed capacity vs on-demand savings.

Appendix: quick T-0 hour-by-hour calendar (local timezone PDT) for the watch crew:
- T-12: final preflight sync (all teams)
- T-2: last staging smoke run and sign-off
- T0 (00:00): Softlaunch open -> 1%
- T0+30m: telemetry check #1 (owner: Ava)
- T0+90m: telemetry check #2, candidate increase to 5% (owner: Liam)
- T0+3h: seeded-eval run (owner: Priya)
- T0+4h..T0+24h: ramp steps every hour as described (owner: Diego)
- T0+24h: post-launch standup and initial notes collection

Notes to self (choppy, TODOs):
- Try short-circuiting routing logs to a lightweight stream for devs to tail without hitting ES cluster.
- Add a small sampling path that records NLU tokens + timing for further model analysis (privacy scrubbed).
- Confirm legal ok on storing sampled prompts for 7 days for debug purposes.

End of draft. Please add real-time annotations in the doc or drop quick comments in #release-ops. If you are assigned an owner above, paste your name and phone (pager) in the collaborator list.
